title: Pietro Schirano (@skirano)
summary:
Some of the reactions to this post are SO expected. Let me walk you through a little journey:
When I started my career, people used Photoshop. I was called crazy for picking up Sketch the moment it came out, tried it, and could never go back.
The whole industry followed.
I was also called crazy when I told people to move from Sketch to Figma.
“I’ll never design in a browser,” I was told.
I could not go back to Sketch because some Figma features were that good.
The whole industry followed.
When I was working at Facebook, I picked up Origami, my favorite tool for prototyping. It pushed my career forward because I became really good at making things that felt real.
The point is, every generation—or every 10 years—there’s a new tool or a new way of doing things. You can either take a leap of faith or fall behind slowly.
The choice is up to you, but ultimately, all that should matter is the final result, no matter what tool you use.
Apple was once notorious for using Keynote for design because they couldn't use any other tool due to security concerns.
Bottom line: If I were starting from scratch again, I could never tell my younger self to learn Figma. That would be a disservice to him.
Quoting @skirano
There is legitimately no reason to use Figma anymore.

When I created Claude Code as a side project back in September 2024, I had no idea it would grow to be what it is today.
